stated_role_or_action: Figured *C. ledgeriana* in his work; selected a tree at Mahanillu for specimens as being botanically a typical Ledger; agreed with Mr. Moens that trees were true Ledgerianas; seen Ceylon and Indian plantations and many mature analyzed trees.
inferred_context: Trimen is a botanist with authority on cinchona plants. His figure is considered by Christie to be accurate, while Howard's is disputed.

stated_role_or_action: Wrote a letter dated June 22nd, 1883, from Lawrence; states he has little to add to Mr. Christie's writing but finds it important; confirms the tree sketched for Dr. Trimen was an undoubted Ledgeriana; states the tree is dead; saw the tree in flower at Mahanillu estate with Mr. Moens and Dr. Trimen; has prints of leaves and bark from the tree itself.
inferred_context: Agar is a resident of Lawrence, Ceylon, and has direct physical access to the specimens (leaves/bark) mentioned. He is a correspondent for The Tropical Agriculturist.

stated_role_or_action: Analyzed bark sent by Mr. Campbell; pronounced it to be Ledgeriana bark, giving 7 per cent of pure quinine (equal to 9 of sulphate) and only a trace of other alkaloids; wrote a paper on the subject; called in the Yarrow Ledgers to help him; supplied Kew with cuttings; gave a plant to Mr. Campbell raised from Ledgeriana seed received from Java.
inferred_context: Howard is a scientist (F.R.S.) based in England, involved in the distribution of cinchona cuttings and seeds. His identification methods are disputed by Christie.

stated_role_or_action: Saw trees in flower at Mahanillu estate; agreed with Dr. Trimen that the trees were true Ledgerianas; his 'idea' of a pure type is referenced by Mr. Campbell; his authority is cited by Mr. Howard regarding the first seed received at Kew.
inferred_context: Moens is an expert on cinchona types, possibly a resident of Ceylon or a frequent visitor, whose opinion is considered authoritative by some, though Howard selectively relies on it.

stated_role_or_action: Sent bark of some trees home for analysis to Mr. Howard; received three rooted cuttings from Kew (supplied by Mr. Howard); wrote to Mr. Christie on 5th instant stating that no one who knows a Ledgeriana tree of a pure type would call his trees Ledgerianas; describes his trees as shrubby, hard shiny leaves, or a broad-leaved Calisaya.
inferred_context: Campbell is based at Lindula, Ceylon. He is a cultivator who has received 'authentic' cuttings but disputes their identity based on appearance.

stated_role_or_action: Wrote a letter dated 7th June 1883, from St. Andrew's, Maskeliya; raised plants from McIvor's seed; planted them on Mahanilu; states the plant Dr. Trimen figured was one he raised; claims other plants from the same seed gave over 12, 13 and 14 per cent sulphate of quinine; has some of Mr. T. Christy's Bolivian plants, 18 months old, and says they are not Ledgers; wrote in the Dikoya essay 9 months ago.
inferred_context: Christie is a cinchona cultivator in Maskeliya with direct knowledge of the seed provenance (McIvor's seed). He is a correspondent for The Tropical Agriculturist.

stated_role_or_action: Provided seed used by Mr. Christie to raise plants.
inferred_context: McIvor is a source of cinchona seed, likely in Ceylon or a related region.

stated_role_or_action: Provided Bolivian calisaya seedlings identified by Mr. Howard as true Ledgerianas; provided Bolivian plants to Mr. Christie.
inferred_context: Christy is a source of Bolivian cinchona plants. His identification of the plants is disputed by Christie.

name_or_description: Analysis of bark by Mr. Howard
stated_role_or_action: Bark from trees at Mahanillu estate was sent home by Mr. Campbell for analysis to Mr. Howard. Howard pronounced it to be Ledgeriana bark, giving 7 per cent of pure quinine (equal to 9 of sulphate) and only a trace of other alkaloids.
inferred_context: The analysis was conducted in England ('sent home'), implying a trans-oceanic scientific collaboration between Ceylon and Britain.

stated_role_or_action: Mr. Christie raised plants from McIvor's seed and planted them on Mahanilu. Mr. Agar planted them. The trees were only about 4½ years old from the time the plants were put out, and were now in a full condition and in flower.
inferred_context: The specific trees in question were cultivated in Ceylon (Mahanillu/Mahanilu) from seed of known provenance.

stated_role_or_action: Other plants, exactly similar in blossom, raised from the same pinch of seed, have given over 12, 13 and 14 per cent sulphate of quinine. The analysis of the tree figured by Dr. Trimen arrived from England and showed 11.29 S.
inferred_context: High quinine yields are used as evidence for the authenticity of the Ledgeriana variety.

stated_role_or_action: In 1876, some seed was received at Kew from Java. Part was communicated to Mr. J. E. Howard, who raised seedlings. He supplied Kew with cuttings. Three of the rooted cuttings were given to Mr. J. A. Campbell of Lindula, Ceylon. Three other plants, imported at Kew from the same authentic strain, were sent to Jamaica.
inferred_context: There was a formal network for distributing 'authentic' cinchona plants between Kew, Ceylon, and Jamaica.

stated_role_or_action: Mr. Christie argues that the 'satin gloss and hairy margin of the leaves' was put forward by Mr. Howard as a characteristic of true Ledgerianas, but Christie states these are common to Ledgeriana and all the Calisayas when young, and not present in mature foliage. Christie identifies Mr. T. Christy's Bolivian calisaya seedlings as not Ledgers, but Calisayas of some kind.
inferred_context: The dispute centers on morphological characteristics vs. chemical analysis and provenance.
